extracted.intended_audience: large companies and their sustainability reporting teams, legal/compliance officers, auditors, investors, civil society and other stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Overview of legal requirements, standards, timelines and policy guidance for corporate sustainability reporting under the EU Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD) and the related European Sustainability Reporting Standards (ESRS). Intended to guide companies on what to report, which standards to use, and when to apply the rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core disclosure requirement: risks, opportunities and impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: EU law requires companies above a certain size to disclose information on what they see as the risks and opportunities arising from social and environmental issues, and on the impact of their activities on people and the environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This helps investors, civil society organisations, consumers and other stakeholders to evaluate the sustainability performance of companies, as part of the European green deal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting standard to use: ESRS
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies subject to the CSRD have to report according to European Sustainability Reporting Standards (ESRS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The standards are developed in a draft form by the EFRAG, previously known as the European Financial Reporting Advisory Group, an independent body bringing together various different stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: First application timing (wave one companies)
rubrics_metrics.description: The first companies subject to the Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD) have to apply the new rules for the first time in the 2024 financial year, for reports published in 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Companies should plan reporting cycles and publication to meet the 2025 public reporting requirement for fiscal year 2024 for wave one.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitional flexibility — 'quick‑fix' delegated act
rubrics_metrics.description: Adoption of a 'quick‑fix' delegated act to revise the first set of ESRS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This revision gives additional flexibility in reporting to wave one companies and ensures that they do not have to report additional information for financial years 2025 and 2026 compared to what they had to report for financial 2024.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postponement mechanism — 'stop‑the‑clock' Directive
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'stop‑the‑clock' Directive postpones the entry into application of the reporting requirements for those companies that were previously required to report for the first time for financial years 2025 or 2026 (wave two and wave three companies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Companies in wave two and wave three should monitor the Directive's application dates to determine their actual first reporting year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope proposal — simplification omnibus (size threshold)
rubrics_metrics.description: Legislative package (Omnibus) proposes to apply the CSRD only to the largest companies (those with more than 1000 employees), focusing the sustainability reporting obligations on the companies which are more likely to have the biggest impacts on people and the environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The package also seeks to ensure that reporting requirements on large companies do not burden smaller companies in their value chains; companies should track legislative changes affecting applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary standard for SMEs (VSME)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation on a voluntary sustainability reporting standard for small and medium-sized undertakings (VSME).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SMEs may use a lighter, voluntary standard rather than full ESRS; the Commission recommends development and use of a VSME standard to suit smaller entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interoperability guidance with global standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on interoperability of European and global sustainability reporting standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission welcomes guidance aimed at ensuring ESRS can interoperate with international/global sustainability reporting frameworks — companies should align disclosures where possible to be consistent with both EU and global expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards development and stakeholder feedback process
rubrics_metrics.description: EFRAG publishes draft ESRS and opens public feedback processes, which the Commission considers before finalising the standards as delegated acts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are formal feedback periods (e.g., public consultations and exposure drafts); stakeholders and companies can engage in the drafting process and should monitor draft publications and consultations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal texts and delegated/implementing acts as compliance sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD) - 2022/2464/EU and the delegated and implementing acts to the CSRD constitute the relevant legislation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Companies must follow the CSRD text and related delegated/implementing acts (and check Official Journal publications and legislative history) to ensure legal compliance; related documents include impact assessments and executive summaries that explain policy intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical guidance and non-mandatory guidelines (NFRD era)
rubrics_metrics.description: Earlier guidelines on non-financial reporting and reporting climate-related information existed (Non-Financial Reporting Directive (NFRD) and accompanying guidelines), and the NFRD was transposed by all EU Member states into national law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although superseded by CSRD/ESRS for many companies, past guidelines and the transposition history remain relevant context for national implementation and for companies transitioning from NFRD reporting to CSRD reporting.
